finding.claim: readBlock() commits the attacker-supplied block length to the field originalLen and decompresses into the shared buffer before the content checksum is verified. When the checksum fails, o and originalLen are left inconsistent, so a caller that catches the IOException and keeps reading gets the unverified decompressed bytes from the failed block returned by read().
finding.source: Attacker-controlled bytes of a compressed block (header originalLen field at line 280, block payload, and checksum field at line 281). Precondition: the application catches the IOException thrown on checksum mismatch and calls read() again on the same stream.
finding.sink: LZ4BlockInputStream.read() returning buffer[o++] (line 204) and read(byte[],int,int) arraycopy (line 220) from data that failed verification.

trace.note: originalLen = readIntLE(header) is assigned to the field before any validation of the decompressed content
buffer reallocated if originalLen is larger than current buffer
decompress writes the block into buffer (safe decompressor path; fast path at line 322)
checksum computed over buffer[0,originalLen) and compared to header check value
on mismatch throws IOException; o is NOT reset and originalLen is NOT rolled back, so the stream state now points at unverified data
next read(): o == originalLen is false (o is the old end of block 1), so no refill happens
read() returns buffer[o++] from the unverified block 2 contents

finding.guards_checked: Magic and method-token checks (lines 268-278); originalLen bounded by 1<<compressionLevel and non-negative (283-285); compressedLen < originalLen unless acceptOversizedBlocks (289); decompressor output length check (318/323); XXHash32 content checksum (336). The checksum is the control that fails open: it is a corruption check, not authentication, so impact is limited to data emitted after an error the caller chose to ignore. Repro: block 1 valid with N1 bytes, read until o==N1; block 2 with valid header, N2 > N1, wrong checksum; catch IOException; read() returns buffer[N1] from block 2. Not executed; verified by reading. Severity: low.

finding.claim: readHeader() replaces this.frameInfo (flags and BD) before the one-byte descriptor hash is verified. After a DESCRIPTOR_HASH_MISMATCH in a non-first frame, read() skips nextFrameInfo() and decodes blocks using the unverified frame's flags while the previous frame's maxBlockSize remains in effect.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled frame descriptor bytes (FLG, BD, optional content size, header hash byte) of a second or later frame. Precondition: the application catches the IOException and keeps reading the same stream.
finding.sink: readBlock() decoding subsequent blocks under unverified FLG.BLOCK_CHECKSUM/CONTENT_CHECKSUM settings (lines 335, 352) and emitting their output via read() (line 373/393).

trace.note: this.frameInfo = new FrameInfo(flg, bd, streamHash) is assigned before any descriptor validation
hash mismatch throws DESCRIPTOR_HASH_MISMATCH; lines 242-246 (maxBlockSize update, firstFrameHeaderRead, anyFrameRead) are skipped
next read(): firstFrameHeaderRead is still true from the prior frame, buffer.remaining()==0 holds
frameInfo.isFinished() is false for the new unverified FrameInfo (assumed; FrameInfo not inspected), so nextFrameInfo() is skipped
readBlock() runs with the unverified flags and the old maxBlockSize

finding.guards_checked: Magic and skippable-frame handling (lines 160-168); FLG/BD validate() reserved-bit and version checks (LZ4FrameOutputStream); 1-byte descriptor hash (232-240), which is a corruption check and is trivially forgeable; per-block size vs maxBlockSize (305); block checksum and content checksum (337, 294) are flag-dependent and so are themselves taken from the unverified header; buffer.limit(0) (244) prevents exposure of prior-block data but does not stop decoding. Verified by reading only; FrameInfo.isFinished default not checked. Severity: low, same defect class as the block-stream finding.
